NVIDIA Quadro NVS 140M (G86) - Win98SE native display driver
Build: 3099  (M5.5 step 8: 800x600 fix - the GDI/GL pitch now equals the hardware scanout pitch at 16/32 bpp (800x600: 1792, not 1600), so GL presents correctly in that mode. Also carries 3098's complete submit drain (nvmini.vxd changed: copy to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM and reboot). 'nvhl heaphi' is a 64 MiB-heap diagnostic only: Half-Life needs ~65 MiB of textures, so sprites loaded last (HUD) fail there.)

Files:
  nvmini.vxd   - display VxD (minivdd) + native G86 backend + 16 KB debug ring
  vmhal9x.dll  - DirectDraw HAL, ring 3 (JHRobotics/vmhal9x, see below) - 3044
  vmdisp9x.dll - its helper DLL (always install both together)
  vmhal3d.dll  - Direct3D DDI 8 part of the HAL (renders through mesa3d.dll)
  mesa3d.dll   - Mesa9x 25.1.6 software OpenGL (llvmpipe), OpenGL ICD + D3D
                 rasterizer; 3046: built here against FBHDA API 20260213
  wgltest.exe, icdtest.exe - Mesa9x test programs (3046)
  nvgl.bat     - 3085: one-shot GPU OpenGL test: clears C:\nvshim.log, sets
                 GALLIUM_DRIVER=nouveau, runs wgltest, opens the log (nvgl sw = llvmpipe)
  d3dsetup.reg - Mesa vector width + OpenGL ICD key for existing installs
  nvmini.drv   - 16-bit DIBENG display driver (3031: VDD device-id probe)
  nvprobe.exe  - Win32 diagnostic/control tool (3034: 'nvprobe log' dumps the ring)
  vmdisp9x.inf - installer (3032: HKR,DEFAULT,DDC,,0; 3033: vesa\Native=1)
  nvsetup.reg  - REGEDIT4 file: Native=1, InitStop=0, BootPattern=0, DDC=0,
                 Mode=16,1024,768 + Config\0001 Display Settings 1024x768x16

Registry (HKLM\Software\vmdisp9x\vesa):
  Native      DWORD  1 = native G86 modeset (DEFAULT since 3033), 0 = vga.drv fallback
  HwCursor    DWORD  1 = G86 hardware cursor (DEFAULT since 3041), 0 = software cursor
  HwCursorScale DWORD 1 = scale cursor positions to the panel in 800x600/640x480
                     (try if the cursor lands in the wrong place in those modes)
  PAT         DWORD  1 = write-combine the aperture through the PAT (DEFAULT since
                     3043), 0 = leave it uncached (MTRR.VXD cannot do it on the T61)
  InitStop    DWORD  debug: stop NV_init_hw_native after stage N (0 = full)
  BootPattern DWORD  1 = draw test bars in the boot modeset (panel diagnostic)

3053: M4.5 r2 - the r1 lost-engine check was not enough. The T61 log of a
screen-off/on showed the resume DID reach our modeset (RestoreDesktopMode ->
SetDisplayMode), but it took the APPEND path and the appended UPDATE never
drained (ntfy=0, get stuck behind put); meanwhile PDISP_OBJECTS and the ch0
DMA_ENABLED bit still read what we programmed, so NV_hw_lost() wrongly said
the engine was fine. The engine was in the old "stuck" state (reads enabled
but will not fetch) - exactly what the full boot init's recovery nudges fix.
r2: a stalled append now DROPS the engine claim and NV_native_modeset RETRIES
once with the full init (RAMHT/channel/preamble/head rebuild + stuck-state
recovery), then restores the cursor. The append wait is capped (fails fast);
NV_hw_lost and the append entry now log the channel registers.
Symptom being chased: after the panel powers off and back on, a blinking
cursor on black then garbage; system stays responsive.
TEST (same as 3052): `nvprobe tail c:\nvtail.txt`, trigger the panel off/on
(or Stand by + resume), and send nvtail.txt. Look for
"append stalled ... dropping engine claim" then
"NV_native_modeset ... OK (full init after stall)".

3052: M4.5 r1 - POWER / SCREEN-SWITCH RECOVERY (first attempt, needs the T61).
Symptom: after standby the desktop does not come back. Mechanism: on resume
the Windows VDD re-POSTs the VGA ROM (_ReInitROM) and the VBIOS reprograms
the display engine; our VxD still believed it owned the EVO core channel and
only APPENDED new head state to a ring nobody executed any more.
- NV_hw_lost(): before every native modeset the VxD checks PDISP_OBJECTS and
  the channel-0 status against what it programmed; a mismatch drops the claim
  and NV_evo_takeover runs the full boot-time init again (RAMHT, channel,
  LUT, head state). The cursor image is re-uploaded from a RAM copy and its
  visibility restored; IA32_PAT entry 1 is re-armed (the BIOS resets it).
- Mini-VDD SET_ADAPTER_POWER_STATE (table index 52) is now implemented and
  logs "SET_ADAPTER_POWER_STATE: devnode=.. state=.." (1 D0 .. 8 D3); the
  VPOWERD Power_Event system message is logged as "Power_Event: n". A D0 or
  resume arms a check ~2 s later: if the engine is still lost and nobody
  restored the desktop, the VxD re-runs the current mode itself and redraws
  everything from the shadow buffer.
- SAVE_REGISTERS / RESTORE_REGISTERS are traced in the log again.
TEST: install nvmini.vxd + nvmini.drv + nvprobe.exe, reboot, start
`nvprobe tail c:\nvtail.txt`, Start -> Shut Down -> Stand by, wait, resume.
Send nvtail.txt (and C:\NVMINI.LOG if the tail died). Also try a full-screen
DOS box (Alt+Enter in a command prompt, then Alt+Enter back) - same mechanism.

3051: OPENGL ICD FIXED FOR REAL (verified 2026-10-23: Half-Life plays in OpenGL
mode on the T61; Direct3D mode plays too, slower with some glitches). Half-Life's "The selected OpenGL mode is not
supported by your video card" (and the same for D3D) was traced with pftest.exe:
the engine asks ChoosePixelFormat() for 24-bit colour / 32-bit depth and refuses
any format flagged PFD_GENERIC_FORMAT without PFD_GENERIC_ACCELERATED, i.e. the
Microsoft "GDI Generic" software OpenGL. That is all Windows offered, because
LoadLibrary(mesa3d.dll) failed (error 31): the 3046 DLL imported CreateHardLinkW,
FindFirstVolumeW, FindNextVolumeW, FindVolumeClose and GetFileSizeEx from KERNEL32,
which do not exist on Windows 98 (pulled in by libstdc++'s std::filesystem via
gallivm/lp_bld_debug.cpp). Reproduced and fixed in a QEMU Win98 SE VM: with the
rebuilt mesa3d.dll the ICD reports 576 pixel formats, Half-Life's request lands
on an accepted one and GL_RENDERER is "llvmpipe (LLVM 18.18, 128 bits)".
Driver binaries unchanged apart from the build stamp. New diagnostics shipped:
  pftest.exe  [W H BPP]  - lists all pixel formats, repeats Half-Life's request
                           and says whether the game would accept it; appends
                           to pftest.txt in the current directory
  pfprobe.exe [dll]      - 3086: repeats GDI ChoosePixelFormat() at each step a driver-mode
                           test takes (fresh, opengl32 loaded, mesa3d loaded, screen
                           created); shows the Win9x 'opengl32 must already be loaded' rule
  icdload.exe [dll]      - does by hand what opengl32.dll does to find/load the
                           ICD (escape, registry, LoadLibrary, DrvValidateVersion,
                           DrvDescribePixelFormat) and prints each step's result
  vmmap.exe              - dumps the process address map (loader debugging)
INSTALL: copy mesa3d.dll (79 MB) over C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM\mesa3d.dll, no reboot
needed; `pftest` should then print GL_RENDERER: llvmpipe. Half-Life: Options ->
Video modes -> OpenGL, Default driver, 640x480.

3050: DCI REFUSED (fixes the Half-Life intro crash; VERIFIED on the T61
2026-10-23: both intros play from the 1024x768x32 desktop, log shows
"DCI(1) refused" at every video open). Root cause
found by bisection on the T61 + disassembly of Win98 SE DIBENG.DLL: the
crash needs (a) a video played by Video for Windows before the game's own
DirectDraw mode switch and (b) one played after it; removing the intro
videos, or starting from a desktop already in the game's mode, avoids it.
nvmini.drv forwarded DCICOMMAND requests with DCI_VERSION to DIBENG, whose
DCICREATEPRIMARYSURFACE fills ONE static, reference-counted DCISURFACEINFO
(width/height/stride/bpp/deBitsOffset/deBitsSelector of the PDevice at
creation) and never refreshes it on a mode change, so DrawDib kept a
1024x768x32 description of a 640x480x16 screen. 3050 answers DCI_VERSION
requests with DCI_FAIL_UNSUPPORTED ("DCI(n) refused" in the log); DrawDib
then falls back to GDI. DirectDraw (DD_VERSION requests) is unaffected.
Cost: Video for Windows playback goes through GDI instead of a direct
framebuffer pointer (slower, but always consistent with the current mode).

3049: LOSSLESS TAIL. Findings so far: Half-Life works when the desktop is
already 640x480x16, and crashes (ring 0) only when it switches there from
1024x768x32 itself; DXDIAG's own 640x480x16 full-screen cycles from the
1024x768x32 desktop work. The 3048 DXDIAG capture lost chunks silently
because the per-blit FBHDA_DD_surface_modify/notify lines (185k of them)
defeated the tail's overlap check. 3049: OP_NV_DBGLOG2 returns the running
byte total ahead of the ring, nvprobe tail appends exactly the new bytes
and writes "[nvprobe tail: N bytes lost]" on overflow; the two per-blit
surface lines are silenced.

3048: MORE DIAGNOSTICS. Both 3047 logs (VxD tail and C:\NVMINI.LOG) end right
after Half-Life's DirectDraw switch to 640x480x16 (ReEnable -> native modeset
OK -> QUERYDIBSUPPORT x3), with no VxD activity visible afterwards. 3048
restarts the per-op traces at every mode change (first 6 calls of each
ring-3 ioctl AND of each PM16 service from the 16-bit driver) and the async
blit timer logs a heartbeat line about once a second (tick, blit count,
pixels, lock count, mode, flags), so the next capture shows whether ring 0
was still running after the switch. nvprobe tail polls every 20 ms.

3047: DIAGNOSTICS. Half-Life (WON) reboots the T61 from "hl.exe -sw -window
-nosound" = a ring-0 failure. The VxD now logs the first 3 calls of every
distinct ring-3 ioctl op (DirectDraw HAL / Mesa requests: op code, input
dwords) and "nvprobe tail <file>" streams the VxD log to a file with
write-through so it survives a reboot. Usage: in a DOS box run
  nvprobe tail c:\nvtail.txt
leave it running, start the program under test, and after the reboot send
c:\nvtail.txt together with c:\nvmini.log (the 16-bit driver's own
on-disk log, appended across boots - the tail is the latest boot).

3046: OPENGL ICD (VERIFIED ON THE T61 2026-10-22: icdtest, wgltest, D3D still
passes). Mesa9x rebuilt from its main branch (commit 8b5428c,
2026-10-04, whose win9x/3d_accel.h is byte-identical to ours) on this Linux
host: LLVM 18.1.8 cross-compiled for mingw32 with Mesa9x's Win9x patch
(file-system/random stubs), then Mesa 25.1.6 llvmpipe (-march=core2,
SSE vectors), with the posix-thread mingw-w64 GCC 13 and Mesa9x's own
winpthreads. The resulting mesa3d.dll replaces the 2025 upstream one, so
its on-screen path reads our FBHDA block correctly and it can serve as the
OpenGL ICD: nvmini.drv reports "SOFTWARE" (OPENGL_GETINFO escape) and
HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\OpenGLdrivers\SOFTWARE
= mesa3d.dll (INF + d3dsetup.reg). Direct3D keeps using the same DLL via
OSMesa. Build recipe: /home/guilherme/projects/mesa9x-build (see
driver/mesa9x-bin/PROVENANCE.txt).
INSTALL: copy mesa3d.dll (replace the 3045 one), wgltest.exe,
icdtest.exe to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM; import d3dsetup.reg; run icdtest.exe
(reports which ICD opengl32 loaded), wgltest.exe (renders through the
ICD), then a 3D screen saver or an OpenGL game. Re-run DXDIAG Test Direct3D to confirm D3D still passes with the new
DLL. If an OpenGL app shows garbage or crashes, report which program and
whether DXDIAG D3D still works (isolates ICD path vs Mesa itself).

3045: DIRECT3D (T61 RESULT 2026-10-22: DirectX 9 runtime, all DXDIAG Direct3D
tests pass; DXDIAG shows 64 MB = the 64 MB shadow buffer (WRAMSize), not the
card's 128 MB - surfaces live in system RAM in this design).
vmhal3d.dll (DDI 8, shipped since 3044) rasterizes through
Mesa9x: it loads mesa3d.dll, prefers the OSMesa API (off-screen rendering,
then copies the colour buffer into the DirectDraw surface). This package now
ships mesa3d.dll from Mesa9x v25.1.6.138 (Mesa 25.1.6 / LLVM 18 llvmpipe,
the newest Mesa9x release; needs SSSE3 = Core 2, which the T61 has).
CAVEAT: that build predates our FBHDA API (20250702 vs 20260213; FBHDA_t
grew after `stride`). Direct3D does not touch that path, but the OpenGL ICD
path inside mesa3d.dll would, so the "SOFTWARE" OpenGL ICD is NOT registered
(OpenGL apps keep Microsoft's software renderer). An ICD needs a Mesa9x
built against our 3d_accel.h - a later job.
TEST ON T61: copy mesa3d.dll to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM (44 MB), import
d3dsetup.reg, run DXDIAG -> Display: Direct3D Acceleration 'Enabled', then
'Test Direct3D' (DX7 and DX8 spinning cube). Then a Direct3D game (software
rasterizer: expect playable at 640x480 for DX6/7-era titles). Copy back
'nvprobe log' and, if vmhal9x wrote one, C:\vmhal9x.log.

3044: DIRECTDRAW (T61 RESULT 2026-10-22: all DXDIAG DirectDraw tests pass).
vmdisp9x's DirectDraw design: DDRAW asks the 16-bit driver
(DCICOMMAND escape) for a 32-bit HAL DLL name; the driver answers vmhal9x.dll,
which DDRAW loads into the application and which drives surfaces through the
VxD's FBHDA API (surfaces live in the shadow, the blitter shows them). All
the VxD and .drv plumbing was already in nvmini; what was missing is the
HAL itself. This package now ships vmhal9x.dll + vmdisp9x.dll (+ vmhal3d.dll)
built from the vmhal9x commit that matches our FBHDA API (20260213; the
August-2025 upstream release DLLs do NOT match and would be refused). The
INF copies them to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM; on an existing install just copy the
three DLLs there yourself (no reboot needed, DDRAW loads them per app).
Also: FBHDA_mode_query returns the native mode table (9 modes @60 Hz)
instead of an empty list.
TEST ON T61: copy the DLLs to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM, run DXDIAG -> Display tab:
DirectDraw Acceleration should read 'Enabled' and 'Test DirectDraw' should
pass (bouncing white box, then full screen). Then any DirectDraw game.
'nvprobe log' / C:\NVMINI.LOG will show 'DDGET32BITDRIVERNAME: success' and
'DDCREATEDRIVEROBJECT: success' (or where it failed).

3043: M4.6b WRITE-COMBINING THROUGH THE PAT (T61 RESULT 2026-10-22: 110 -> 6-7
cycles/pixel, full-screen blit ~2 ms, window dragging smooth; IA32_PAT entry 1
was already WC - MTRR.VXD had set it but never marked the pages). 3042's counters on the T61:
MTRR.VXD refuses the WC request (rc C0000001) because the BIOS marks the
whole PCI hole C0000000-FFFFFFFF UC in MTRR0, and UC beats any overlapping
WC MTRR. Result: ~110 cycles per pixel, ~40 ms for a full-screen blit (the
blit timer runs every 16 ms). The fast path alone changed nothing - the bus
was the bottleneck. Fix: MTRR UC + PAT WC = WC (Intel SDM 11.12). The VxD
now sets IA32_PAT entry 1 (PWT=1: 'write-through', unused by Win98) to WC
with the SDM cache-disable sequence and sets PWT in the page-table entries
of OUR 24 MB aperture mapping only, after verifying every entry's frame is
the expected BAR1 page (PTE walk via CR3 + _MapPhysToLinear). The blitter
issues sfence after each blit so the EVO code's uncached VRAM alias never
sees stale data. Registry PAT=0 disables it. 'nvprobe mtrr' now prints the
PAT state, IA32_PAT and correct MTRR sizes (3042 ignored the valid bit and
the 36-bit physical address width).
TEST ON T61: desktop as before; 'nvprobe mtrr' before and after ~10 s of
dragging a window with 'show contents while dragging'; expect
'PAT: APPLIED', entry1=WC, and cycles/pixel well below 110 (hope: <10).
If the screen corrupts or the machine freezes right after the desktop
appears, boot Safe Mode and add PAT=0 to HKLM\Software\vmdisp9x\vesa.

3042: M4.6 SHADOW-BLIT PERFORMANCE. The shadow blitter (wram -> VRAM) used
two indirect calls per pixel; it now copies whole rows with rep movsd when
the shadow and scanout layouts match (16->16, 32->32) and uses tight loops
for 8->32 (palette), 8->16, 16->32 and 32->16. The generic per-pixel path
stays for gamma ramps, the software cursor and integer-scaled VESA modes.
Dirty rectangles were already in place (GDI's BeginAccess rect -> one
bounding box per 16 ms timer tick). Write-combining on the aperture was
already requested from MTRR.VXD but never checked; the result is now logged
and 'nvprobe mtrr' dumps the CPU's variable MTRRs (rdmsr in the VxD) so we
can see whether E0000000 (24 MB - not a power of two) really got WC, plus
blit counters (TSC cycles per blit / per pixel).
TEST ON T61: desktop works as before; run 'nvprobe mtrr' once, drag a window
around for ~10 s, run it again; copy both outputs + 'nvprobe log'. Expect
'fast path' == blits and the aperture listed as type WC.

3041: M4.4 HARDWARE CURSOR (T61 RESULT 2026-10-22: works). The mouse pointer is now the G86's own 64x64
A8R8G8B8 cursor (nouveau nv50_cursor.c recipe): the image is built from the
Windows AND/XOR masks into VRAM at 0x1830000, shown/hidden through the core
channel (head0 methods 0x89C=ctxdma, 0x880=0x85000000/0x05000000, 0x884=
offset>>8, then UPDATE), moved through the cursor PIO channel (0x647084 /
0x647080). Screen-invert pixels (AND=1, XOR=1 - the I-beam) draw as black.
The software cursor is no longer composited by the shadow blitter, so moving
the mouse no longer costs a blit. The core ring now wraps with a JUMP-to-0
(nouveau evo_wait) instead of refusing after ~20 mode sets.
Fallbacks: HwCursor=0 restores the software cursor; HwCursorScale=1 scales
the position in the scaled modes if the pointer is offset there.
TEST ON T61: pointer visible at 1024x768 and tracks the mouse; shape changes
(arrow / I-beam over text / hourglass / resize arrows); pointer still right
after switching to 800x600 and back; 'nvprobe log' shows 'NV_cursor_load:
... -> OK'. If the pointer is invisible or garbage, report whether Windows
still responds to clicks (the cursor is then at the right place but unseen).

3040: M4.1 FIX - 800x600 True Color came up as garbage (Windows reverted after
15 s). Cause: NV50 linear scanout surfaces need a 256-byte-aligned pitch
(nouveau_fbcon rounds up to 256); 800x4=3200 and 800x2=1600 are not, while
1024- and 640-pixel rows happen to be. NV_hw_pitch() now rounds the scanout
pitch up (800x600x32 -> 3328); the shadow keeps its exact pitch and the
blitter's dst_pitch carries the padding.
T61 RESULT 2026-10-22: all modes tested, all fine (640x480, 800x600, 1024x768
at 256/High/True color). M4.1 DONE.

3039: M4.1 MODE LIST + M4.2 INF-ONLY INSTALL.
 M4.1 - native modes are now 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768 at 8, 16 and 32 bpp
   (NV_mode_ok). The panel raster stays the fixed 1024x768@60 LVDS timing;
   800x600/640x480 framebuffers are stretched to it by the head scaler
   (nouveau nv50_crtc_set_scale: SCALE_CTRL 0x8A4=9, SCALE_RES1/2 = 1024x768,
   0x8C8 = input size). 8 bpp desktops scan out as 32 bpp: the shadow (wram)
   is 8 bpp and the blitter expands it through the palette (readpx8), so no
   hardware CLUT is involved. 24 bpp stays rejected by ValidateMode.
 M4.2 - the INF now also binds the root VGA devnode (*PNP0900), which is where
   the T61 runs the adapter, so a plain Have Disk install needs no tricks.
   Everything nvsetup.reg sets is already written by the INF (drv, minivdd,
   Mode 16,1024,768, DDC=0, Native=1); nvsetup.reg is now a repair tool, and
   SYSTEM.INI can stay at display.drv=pnpdrvr.drv (KERNEL resolves it through
   the VDD once the devnode is bound - verified in the QEMU harness).
TEST ON T61: install the three 3039 files, reboot, then in Display Properties
check the list (should offer 640x480/800x600/1024x768 at 256/High/True color),
try 800x600 True Color (expect a stretched desktop) and 1024x768 256 colors
(expect a normal-looking desktop; icons may show palette artifacts in 256).
Collect nvprobe log after each switch: 'native mode set: WxHxB ... (scaled)'.
If a mode comes up black, the panel still has the native timing: press OK /
wait 15 s for the Windows revert, or switch back in Safe Mode.

3038: M4.3 NATIVE MEMORY SETUP (first M4 item after E4). CONFIRMED ON THE T61
2026-10-22: PFB reports 128 MB (cfg0 01001800 cfg1 01449000), window 24 MB,
layout OK, native 1024x768x32 desktop unchanged.
 - The scanout window handed to the shadow blitter is no longer a fixed 12 MB:
   it is min(VRAMLimit MB, PCI BAR1 size, NVFB_WINDOW_MAX=24 MB), i.e. 24 MB
   by default, which leaves room for three 1024x768x32 flip buffers.
 - NV_vram_check() (vxd_nv.c) reads the real VRAM size from PFB 0x10020C
   (nouveau nv50_vram.c decode) plus PFB cfg0/cfg1, and validates the layout
   in nv50_evo.h: window < EVO reservation (24 MB), VRAM >= 32 MB + 32 KiB
   (RAMIN end). It runs in LIVE VM context only (first call from the
   mini-VDD register handler, i.e. DriverInit; also lazily before any native
   mode set) because BAR0 access inside Device_Init freezes the G86.
 - NV_native_modeset refuses to run if the check failed, so a wrong card or
   layout logs a reason instead of scribbling EVO structures into VRAM.
 - nvprobe (no arguments) now prints VRAM size, cfg regs, window and the
   check result; 'nvprobe log' shows the NV_vram_check lines.
TEST ON T61: install the three 3038 files, reboot, run  nvprobe  and
nvprobe log > nvlog.txt. Expect 'NV_vram_check: VRAM 128 MB ... window 24 MB'
and 'layout OK' right after 'register: ebx = 1', desktop unchanged.

3037: *** ROOT CAUSE OF EVERY 'LoadFail = nvmini.drv 0000' SINCE M1 - FIXED ***
CONFIRMED ON THE T61 2026-10-22: LoadSuccess = nvmini.drv, native EVO modeset
1024x768x32 at boot, desktop usable, Display Properties can change depth.
nvmini.drv never ran: Win98 KERNEL rejected the NE image before calling
DriverInit. init.c declared `extern char __based(__segname("_TEXT")) *pText`
and locked (__segment)pText. Current Open Watcom compilers treat "_TEXT" in
__segname() as a user DATA segment: they emit an empty FAR_DATA segment named
_TEXT, wlink drops it, and the .drv keeps a SEGMENT relocation to non-existent
segment 3 (see tools: `python3 -I <scratch>/nerelocs.py nvmini.drv`). The
loader fails the fixup -> LoadModule error 0 -> vga.drv. Upstream's 2023-era
toolchain did not do this, which is why the official release loads.
Fix: GlobalSmartPageLock(get_cs()) with `#pragma aux get_cs = "mov ax,cs"`.
Proven in a QEMU Win98SE harness: with the fix, vesamini.drv (same 16-bit
objects) logs 'D> DriverInit: ENTER', connects to the VxD, and brings up a
1024x768x16 desktop. Also in 3037: the 16-bit driver is linked with the
2025-08 Open Watcom (the Oct-2026 wlink snapshot ignores 'segment type data
preload fixed'; the makefile now also names class DATA/BSS explicitly), the
DIBENG mini driver's NE now matches the official layout (flags 8201, FIXED
DGROUP, no data-segment entries). dbg output additionally mirrored to I/O
port E9h (QEMU -debugcon), harmless on real hardware.
TEST ON T61: copy nvmini.drv + nvmini.vxd + nvprobe.exe (3037). Keep SYSTEM.INI
display.drv=nvmini.drv (direct name is fine now; pnpdrvr.drv also works once
the devnode is bound) and the nvsetup.reg values. Reboot. Expect BOOTLOG
'LoadSuccess = nvmini.drv' and the native 1024x768x16 desktop. Then collect
nvprobe log > nvlog.txt (now full of 'D>' lines) and BOOTLOG.TXT.

3035: SECOND LOG CHANNEL + more VxD breadcrumbs. The 3034 ring from the T61
showed a healthy VxD (native init OK, Device_Init DONE) but NOT ONE 'D> ' line
and no 'register:' line: the 16-bit driver reached neither the VxD PM16 API
nor our mini-VDD table. To see the 16-bit side regardless, nvmini.drv now
ALSO appends every dbg line to C:\NVMINI.LOG (KERNEL _lopen/_lwrite, max 600
lines per boot session; delete the file to start clean). The VxD additionally
logs: the VDD mini dispatch table length (handlers installed only if >= 0x31),
the first PM16 API call it receives, any unknown PM16 service number, and the
arrival of OP_FBHDA_SETUP.
TEST: copy the three files, reboot, then collect  nvprobe log > nvlog.txt,
C:\NVMINI.LOG, BOOTLOG.TXT (logged boot) and the live C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM.INI.

3034: DEBUG LOG WITHOUT A SERIAL PORT. DBGPRINT is now compiled in, but the
sink is a 16 KB ring buffer inside nvmini.vxd (dbgring.h) instead of COM1:
  V> ...   lines printed by the VxD (Device_Init, VESA/native init, mini-VDD
           register handler, mode set hooks)
  D> ...   lines printed by nvmini.drv (DriverInit, VXD connect per device id,
           FBHDA, PhysicalEnable/SetDisplayMode), pushed one character at a
           time through the VxD PM16 API (OP_NV_DBG_PUTC)
Read it after the boot with:   nvprobe log > nvlog.txt
It survives the vga.drv fallback (the VxD stays loaded). As with lastset: if
BOOTLOG has no 'Dynamic load device nvmini.vxd', nvprobe loads a fresh VxD and
the ring only holds that fresh instance's init. Nothing is written to disk at
boot. Ops: OP_NV_DBGLOG 0x500A (W32 ioctl), OP_NV_DBG_PUTC 0x500B (PM16).
TEST: copy nvmini.vxd/.drv/nvprobe.exe (3034), SYSTEM.INI (no IgnoreRegistry),
merge nvsetup.reg, reboot, then:  nvprobe log > nvlog.txt  and send it with
BOOTLOG.TXT. First expected lines: 'D> DriverInit: ENTER (nvmini.drv build
3034)' followed by 'D> VDD_REGISTER_DISPLAY_DRIVER_INFO for device id: N' and
'V> register: ebx = N ...' - the exact point DriverInit gives up.

FIELD NOTE 2026-10-21: do NOT use [display] IgnoreRegistry=1 in SYSTEM.INI.
The Win98 VDD reads the same key (VDD_PNP_Load_MiniVDD) and, when set, skips
loading DEFAULT\minivdd -> nvmini.vxd never loads, nvmini.drv DriverInit
fails (LoadFail 0000) and Windows is on vga.drv. Set the desktop mode through
the registry instead (nvsetup.reg now writes Config\0001\Display\Settings
1024x768x16 and DEFAULT\Mode=16,1024,768); keep x_resolution/y_resolution/bpp
in [Display] only as the fallback. dist/driver/SYSTEM.INI is the reference.

3033: Native=1 is now the built-in default (no registry value needed); set
Native=0 to get the safe vga.drv boot. The INF also writes Native=1, and
nvsetup.reg sets everything in one go: double-click it on the T61 (or
`regedit /s nvsetup.reg`). It assumes the adapter's class key is
Class\Display\0000 - check in regedit that 0000\DEFAULT holds
minivdd=nvmini.vxd; if your NVIDIA key is 0001 etc., edit the path in the file.

3032: SLOW-BOOT FIX + three static-review fixes (on top of 3031).
 a) ~3 min boot: BOOTLOG tick stamps put 173 of the ~181 s of the VxD phase
    inside CONFIGMG "Enumerating NVIDIA Quadro NVS 140M" -> "Enumerated". That
    is the Win98 VDD's monitor enumerator reading the EDID itself through INT
    10h AX=4F15 in V86 mode (no mini-VDD GET_MONITOR_INFO); the G86 VBIOS
    under V86 crawls. The VDD skips the probe when HKR\DEFAULT\DDC is "0":
    added to vmdisp9x.inf ([NV.AddReg]; the shared [VM.AddReg] wrote DDC=1, so
    the T61 registry currently says 1). Without reinstalling, CHANGE it with
    regedit: HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Class\Display\000N\DEFAULT
      (the key holding minivdd=nvmini.vxd): String value DDC: 1 -> 0
 b) native setmode never armed the blitter: VESA_draw() bailed on vga_mode /
    act_mode, so a successful handshake would have shown a black desktop.
 c) Native=0 with display.drv=nvmini.drv: register_display_driver dereferenced
    hda==NULL once 3031's id probe made it reachable. Now returns zeros ->
    clean vga.drv fallback (VRAM slot[3]=0x302 marks that case).
 d) EVO takeover claims nv_owned only after a completed commit.
TEST: regedit DDC=0 (or reinstall INF), copy the three files, Native=1, reboot.
Expect: VxD phase seconds instead of minutes, desktop 1024x768x16 on nvmini.drv.

3031: THE DRIVERINIT FIX (from Win98SE VDD.VXD disassembly, 98 DDK symbols).
The Win98 VDD keys every display-driver call on EBX as a DISPLAY DEVICE ID
(1..N), not a VM handle. Id 1 = the devnode the VDD considers "the VGA" and
is served by the global mini-VDD dispatch table. A mini-VDD the VDD loads for
any OTHER display devnode is moved into that device's private table and the
global table is restored (VDD _LoadMiniVDD). The upstream vmdisp9x .drv
always registers with EBX = VM id = 1, so on this T61 - where the ghost
"Standard PCI Graphics Adapter (VGA)" is id 1 and the NVIDIA devnode is id 2 -
the register call hit an empty table, EDX stayed 0, DriverInit returned 0.
nvmini.drv now tries VDD_REGISTER_DISPLAY_DRIVER_INFO with ids 1..4 and keeps
the first id whose mini-VDD returns an FBHDA alias for all later VDD calls.
The VxD logs that id right after the 0x300 marker (slot [1]).
TEST: same SYSTEM.INI as before (display.drv=nvmini.drv, [display] 1024x768
bpp=16 IgnoreRegistry=1), Native=1, replace the three files, reboot.
Expect the desktop at 1024x768x16 on nvmini.drv. If it still falls back:
  nvprobe vramrd 0x1900000 16  -> slot[0]=B0070100, slot[1]=device id,
  slot[3]=0x301/0x302. BOOTLOG.TXT "LoadFail = nvmini.drv" code tells the rest.

3030: boot-handshake VRAM trace. With display.drv=nvmini.drv the 16-bit driver
now LOADS at boot (file-found; pnpdrvr.drv was missing -> that was the earlier
LoadFail 0002), but its DriverInit returns 0 => "LoadFail nvmini.drv 0000" and
Windows falls back to vga.drv. lastset shows hook branch 0 (setmode never
reached), so DriverInit fails in the VxD connect handshake, before any modeset.
register_display_driver (the mini-VDD side of the driver's
VDD_REGISTER_DISPLAY_DRIVER_INFO call) now resets the VRAM boot log and logs how
far the handshake gets. Diagnostic procedure:
  1. nvprobe vramfill 0x1900000 16 0        (pre-clear the log)
  2. reboot (Native=1) -> it falls back to vga.drv as before
  3. nvprobe vramrd 0x1900000 16
     [0]=B0070100 magic -> register_display_driver WAS reached
       (absent/all-zero -> handshake dies BEFORE our mini-VDD)
     then 0x300, raw hda ptr, 0x301(ok)/0x302(null), hda_pm16, mouse_pm16,
     vram_pm16 selectors.
